name: Maya Bell
preparty_markdown:
Maya is responsible for making the museum intelligible to people who did not spend twelve years specializing

in one dynasty. Warm, quick, and occasionally subversive, she can turn an academic argument into a great

tour question and a donor speech into something children will actually remember.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Engaging, practical, empathetic, irreverent about institutional pomp.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Close to Beatrice Plinth, who champions the education program.

• Often rescues Sebastian Reed from awkward public-facing moments.

• Works with Celeste Frame to translate scholarship into gallery interpretation.

COSTUME

Colorful cocktail attire or polished museum-professional look, comfortable shoes, fun brooch or earrings, optional stack of

tour cards.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“If the label needs a semicolon, we have already lost the fifth graders.”

“Museums are for people. I have checked the bylaws.”

name: Avery Lens
preparty_markdown:
Avery photographs artists, collectors, and public figures for magazines that describe parties like tonight as

'intimate' despite inviting two hundred people. They are quiet when working, socially fluent when not, and

very good at being present without becoming the center of the frame.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Observant, understated, curious, visually minded. You notice who is standing with whom and what happens at the edge of a

room.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Has photographed several investigations for Nadia Quill.

• Imogen Muse loves Avery's work because Avery does not overdirect.

• Daphne Palette always knows which side Avery is shooting from.

COSTUME

Elegant all-black or dark cocktail wear, camera as the key prop if available, comfortable shoes, press-style shoulder bag.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“People become very honest when they think I am photographing someone else.”

“Do that again, but less aware of your jawline.”

name: Juno March
preparty_markdown:
Juno campaigns for museums and collectors to return contested cultural objects, publish complete

provenance, and stop treating possession as the end of the conversation. She is articulate, strategic, and

much more interested in leverage than theatrics—although she knows theatrics can create leverage.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Focused, bold, principled, socially savvy. Challenge people without turning every conversation into a speech.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Frequently debates Marcus Pryce and Vivienne Marrow on strategy.

• Everett Locke has removed Juno from a museum event before; both remember it.

• Maya Bell quietly agrees with more of Juno's critique than museum leadership suspects.

COSTUME

Smart gala attire with activist edge: bold pin, statement scarf, printed tote, elegant suit or dress. Avoid costume-protester

clichés.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“A glass case is not a moral argument.”

“I brought talking points. I did not bring a megaphone. Growth.”
